title: Volume 1 - Chapter 8: Envy
content: Chapter 8: Envy
Allison and Dr. Smith, who had been summoned by the upper management, were asserting the continuation of the project before the executives. At this moment, Dr. Smith was speaking about the plan.
“We have confirmed a slight output of magic power. Also, although temporary, there has been an increase in magic power output, so I insist that the experiments must continue.”

In the meeting room where only dismal results had been presented so far, the executives’ eyes were cold as they looked at the smiling Dr. Smith. Allison had thought that scrapping the project was inevitable, but the upper management—the executives leading the Prometheus Project—felt otherwise.
“These numbers aren’t enough to justify continuing the project. Dr. Smith, what we want are tangible results.”
“I understand.”

Dr. Smith replied with a smile, which seemed to infuriate the executives. They seemed to want to ask if he understood the critical situation. But Dr. Smith was famously eccentric. Perhaps realizing it was pointless to argue, they wanted to move the discussion forward. Allison, for once, was grateful to Dr. Smith for saving them from wasting time.
One of the executives sighed exaggeratedly before speaking.
“The humanoid weapon development project was once abolished due to its ineffectiveness against the Gijuu. This Prometheus Project is essentially a restart for us.”
By coming to this meeting, Allison finally understood why the magic power converter was installed in the humanoid weapon.
(The members of the humanoid weapon development team have regrouped for a revenge attempt. They’re really persistent.)

It was a ridiculous reason for equipping the humanoid weapon instead of a fighter jet or a tank. It wasn’t that the humanoid weapon had no advantages at all, but there must have been better methods—though Allison remained silent, watching the meeting unfold.
The executive continued.
“At the time, we were mocked for spending a huge budget on a toy. If this fails, we will never get another chance. Please understand that.”
Like the executives, they themselves would never get another chance. Dr. Smith looked troubled and asked the executives.
“How long do you expect us to produce results?”
The highest-ranking man among the executives answered.

“I’d say by the end of the year, but realistically, three months. Beyond that, we can’t protect you. Many are skeptical about the Prometheus Project. Above all, the Valkyries are opposed. We want at least ten percent of the maximum output achieved. Without visible results, we can’t persuade them.”

Many of the executives were women, most of whom were former Valkyries. Nearly half a century had passed since the Gijuu first appeared, and Valkyries had taken powerful positions within the organization. The executives gathered here were probably in a tough spot.
Hearing the three-month deadline, Dr. Smith sought confirmation.
“Would it be acceptable to use somewhat rough methods? Increasing the proportion of Gijuu cells in test pilots would simply raise magic power output.”
The executives knew what Dr. Smith’s proposal implied. They knew, but still gave him permission.
“Permission granted.”
The executives were cornered and, if there was a chance, allowed inhumane methods. Allison lowered her head and clenched her hands tightly during the meeting.

The experimental machine, Thunderbolt, returned to the hangar. I, having changed into my pilot suit, was briefing with Dr. Allison before boarding the machine. We confirmed the details of this experiment and the changes made to the experimental machine.

On the ground, adjustments had been made not only to the magic power converter’s output but also to the Thunderbolt’s airframe itself. It seemed to be a modification to operate the magic power converter more efficiently.
“The appearance hasn’t changed, has it?”
“The modifications are internal and software-based. We didn’t have the luxury to change the exterior.”
Dr. Allison, holding a tablet device, finished explaining everything to me and then wore a gloomy expression. She also told me how I would be treated if this experiment failed.
“If this experiment fails, you’ll be sent back to the ground. They plan to amputate your healthy limbs to increase magic power output.”

I had somewhat expected this. Because of the repeated failures, they were desperate to produce results. Even though they knew replacing my limbs with Gijuu parts wouldn’t significantly increase output, they intended to proceed. But I was not in a position to refuse.
“…Understood.”

Having accepted this, Dr. Allison glared at me with teary eyes. Unlike when Lieutenant Hayase glared at me before, I didn’t feel scared at all. Even though she was still a teenager, Hayase’s gaze was astonishing even now. There were soldiers on the ground with similar eyes, but almost all of them were veterans.
Dr. Allison seemed displeased with my attitude.
“Do you think the surgery will go smoothly? Even now, your success rate isn’t high. At worst, you could die or never get up again. Are you sure you want to go through with it?”
“I will. It’s my duty as a volunteer.”
“…I see. You’re obedient to orders to the very end. You’re really a convenient soldier.”
There was some truth in Dr. Allison’s sarcasm. But this time, I had a little confidence. No, it wasn’t confidence.
“If this fails, I’ll be able to accept it.”
Climbing the ladder prepared for entering the cockpit, Dr. Allison looked at me suspiciously.
“You seem unusually calm today. Did something happen while we were away?”
“Yes, I received advice from an unexpected person.”
Dr. Allison tilted her head but seemed to have no time to confirm who it was and returned to her post.
“I hope this time it succeeds.”
Since I had failed due to Louise’s advice, she seemed resigned to low expectations this time as well.
Sliding into the cockpit, I took a deep breath to steady myself.
“Face forward and take one step at a time… that’s all I need right now.”
I muttered words my mother had taught me, applying them to myself. For now, I just had to confront the problem in front of me. Do what I could… and if I failed, so be it.
“My life is already over. I don’t regret it anymore. But… if I could fly like a Valkyrie, I would…”
Gripping the control stick quietly but firmly, Dr. Smith’s face appeared on the monitor.
“Then let’s begin. Are you ready, Envy?”
“Yes. Whenever you are.”
“Then the test begins. Start outputting your magic power. Oh, and don’t get too worked up. Even if you fail, you’ll just have surgery and rehab.”
“…Understood.”

For me, this was a life-or-death matter, but for Dr. Smith, it seemed trivial. He appeared gentle and kind but also showed a cruel side. He probably wasn’t even aware of his cruelty. Without someone like Dr. Smith, I wouldn’t have had this chance.

As the test started, the magic power output appeared on the monitor as a number. The output showed zero, but when I channeled magic power into the control stick, the number rose. The number was displayed in red, indicating a failed experiment.
I could hear Dr. Allison and the development team’s conversation through the comms.
“There’s not much change from last time.”
“No, it’s slightly higher than last time.”
The number kept rising. Dr. Allison seemed to sense something strange.
“The number keeps rising? Is there a problem with the measuring device?”
“We’ve checked it many times; it’s fine.”

The number on the monitor continued to climb. Inside the cockpit, I recalled Lieutenant Hayase’s words. I faced the honest feelings inside me. I envied the Valkyries, watching them in the battlefield sky, longing for the power to fly freely and slaughter Gijuu. When I confronted those genuine feelings, the magic power seemed to respond.
“Now that I think about it, Envy was a fitting callsign for me.”

Accepting my jealousy toward the Valkyries, the magic power output continued to rise. I felt magic power overflowing from the limbs and organs transplanted into my body, wrapped in a sense of exhilaration.
“This is the feeling of drawing out magic power! With this strength, I—”

—My inner voice leaked out in excitement. But before I could say more, I regained my composure. At the same time, I forgot what I was about to say. Rather than forgetting, it’s more accurate to say I didn’t even know what I was going to say.
Though I was glad to finally be able to fight the Gijuu properly, it didn’t feel like I could actually defeat them. What was I about to say?
While I was thinking, the output surpassed the passing mark of ten percent. Dr. Smith, probably excited, brought his face close to the camera. His face filled the entire frame on the monitor.
“We’ve reached it! Magic power output is maintaining fifteen percent. Envy’s magic power output has greatly exceeded the target. This means the project can move to the next stage!”

Dr. Smith, joyfully innocent, was as excited as a child. I, gripping the control stick, was also a little surprised by the result. Despite all the struggles, coughing up blood and bloody urine, I had easily surpassed the ten percent magic power output target.

“Magic power output is stable. Now the force field can protect the machine! If we divert surplus energy to buoyancy, the humanoid weapon can achieve fighter jet-level speed and mobility. Deployment for combat testing is near!”
Dr. Smith’s excitement was interrupted by Dr. Allison, who, while surprised, kept a calm facade.
“…There isn’t enough energy left for weapons. Combat testing is premature.”
“Ah, we rushed a bit. But with these results, upper management will likely allocate budget to the Prometheus Project. Our future looks bright, Allison.”
Hearing those words about a bright future, Dr. Allison responded coldly.
“I feel the bright future has moved further away… Envy, the experiment was a success. Stop the magic power output and take a short break. We’ll conduct another test in fifteen minutes.”
“Understood.”
After ending the communication, I let out a deep sigh inside the cockpit and looked upward.
“…What was I about to say?”
Amid the joy of having achieved the set goal, a slight unease arose. I tried to find an answer during the break, but Dr. Allison called me back to the experiment immediately.
